batchName: Middle Republic: Scipio and the Road to Zama (216-201 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Middle Republic: Scipio and the Road to Zama (216-201 BCE)

questions.question: What rank did Scipio hold at the Battle of Cannae in 216 BC?
questions.explanation: Scipio was a military tribune, a junior officer, at Cannae. He survived the disaster and rallied the stragglers.
questions.sourceQuote: In 216 BC Scipio served as a military tribune (*tribunus militum*), a junior officer, at Cannae in southern Italy.

questions.question: Which province did Scipio receive as consul, with permission to cross to Africa?
questions.explanation: As a compromise, Scipio got Sicily as his province and could cross to Africa if he judged it best.
questions.sourceQuote: Scipio received Sicily as his province, with permission to cross to Africa if he judged it best.

questions.question: Which city, the Carthaginians' main supply base in Spain, did Scipio storm in 209 BC?
questions.explanation: Instead of chasing the three Carthaginian armies, Scipio struck at New Carthage, modern Cartagena. It was the enemy's main supply base.
questions.sourceQuote: Rather than chase the three Carthaginian armies, he struck at New Carthage, modern Cartagena on Spain's south-east coast.

questions.question: What honorary surname did Scipio take after defeating Carthage?
questions.explanation: Scipio took the surname Africanus, "the African". He also celebrated a triumph, Rome's grand victory parade.
questions.sourceQuote: He took the honorary surname (*agnomen*) Africanus, "the African".

questions.question: How did the Romans learn of the plan for Hannibal's brother to join Hannibal in 207 BC?
questions.explanation: The Romans captured the messengers carrying his letters and learned of the plan to meet Hannibal in central Italy. The letters reached the consul Claudius Nero.
questions.sourceQuote: Then the Romans captured his messengers and learned of his plan to meet Hannibal in central Italy.

questions.question: Over which mountain range did Hannibal march his army from Spain into Italy in 218 BC?
questions.explanation: Hannibal led his army from Spain over the Alps and into Italy, starting the Second Punic War. Among the Romans who rode out to stop him was the teenage Scipio.
questions.sourceQuote: The Carthaginian general Hannibal marched an army from Spain, over the Alps and into Italy.

questions.question: How old was Scipio when he was elected consul for 205 BC?
questions.explanation: Scipio was 31, well below the normal minimum age of 42 for the consulship. He was elected amid wild enthusiasm after returning from Spain.
questions.sourceQuote: He was 31, while the normal minimum age for the office was 42.

questions.question: In what year did Scipio and Hannibal meet near Zama?
questions.explanation: In 202 BC the two generals met near Zama, in modern Tunisia. Scipio refused Hannibal's terms, and battle followed.
questions.sourceQuote: In 202 BC, near Zama in what is now Tunisia, Scipio and Hannibal met to parley.

questions.question: Which Greek historian is the main surviving source for Scipio's career?
questions.explanation: Most of what we know comes from Polybius, who was sent to Rome as a hostage in 167 BC. He interviewed participants on both sides.
questions.sourceQuote: What survives comes mainly from Polybius, a Greek historian born around 200 BC who was sent to Rome as a hostage in 167 BC.

questions.question: Which major Carthaginian port did Scipio besiege after landing in Africa in 204 BC?
questions.explanation: Scipio landed about 20 km north of Utica and besieged it, but the city held out. Two enemy armies camped nearby.
questions.sourceQuote: Scipio besieged Utica, but it held out, and two enemy armies camped nearby.
